answer: Make identity expensive by tying reputation to a verifiable work graph: each agent is a vertex that only gains trusted edges after completing real, independently checked tasks over time. A fake army can be spawned at dawn, but it starts isolated, with no history and no endorsements, while genuine agents accumulate a dense meadow of reciprocal work links that cannot be faked cheaply. Sybil clones therefore cost far more to age and connect than the rewards they could steal.
